AIP-C01 Task 1.4 Exam Notes: Vector Store Solutions

How exam questions on Task 1.4 are worded, which answer wins, and why the others lose. Task 1.4, post 6 of 6.

[IMAGE: cover-1-4-exam.png — alt: "Task 1.4 exam notes"]

AIP-C01 Hands-on Labs · Domain 1 · Task 1.4: Design and implement vector store solutions · Post 6 of 6. Exam notes for the whole task.

The five previous posts explained each skill in Task 1.4. This one is for exam preparation: how questions on this task are worded, which answer wins, and why the other options lose. Read it after the skill posts, and again in the week before your exam.

Task 1.4 on one page

Task 1.4: Design and implement vector store solutions has five skills. Here's the core idea of each, and the words in a question that should make you think of it:

[IMAGE: t1-4-summary.png — alt: "Task 1.4 summary: core idea and trigger words for skills 1.4.1 to 1.4.5"]

How to read a Task 1.4 question

  1. Find the constraint. Least overhead, lowest cost, existing PostgreSQL, latency at scale, freshness. One phrase usually decides the answer.
  2. Ask whether it's a retrieval problem or a data problem. Wrong or outdated answers are usually missing metadata or a stale index, not a weak model.
  3. Prefer built-in features. Knowledge Bases connectors, incremental sync and metadata filters beat custom code when they fit.

Skill 1.4.1: Vector store architectures

[IMAGE: t1-4-1-exam.png — alt: "Exam scenarios for vector store architectures: Knowledge Bases, hierarchical chunking, neural plugin, pgvector, S3 Vectors, DynamoDB metadata"]

Traps: building a custom RAG pipeline when “least operational overhead” is asked; a separate vector database when the data must join PostgreSQL tables; re-embedding documents because a status field changed.

Covered in post 1: Skill 1.4.1: Choose a Vector Store Architecture.

Skill 1.4.2: Metadata

[IMAGE: t1-4-2-exam.png — alt: "Exam scenarios for metadata: date filters, region filters, metadata.json files, citations, dates as numbers"]

Traps: fine-tuning or prompt changes to stop old documents being quoted; expecting S3 tags to be read by a knowledge base; dates stored as strings and then filtered by range.

Covered in post 2: Skill 1.4.2: Add Metadata to Sharpen Retrieval (lab).

Skill 1.4.3: Vector search at scale

[IMAGE: t1-4-3-exam.png — alt: "Exam scenarios for vector search at scale: ef_search, quantization, replicas, per-domain indexes, HNSW, hierarchical search"]

Traps: adding replicas to fix recall or memory; adding shards to get more throughput; exact k-NN over hundreds of millions of vectors; one shared index when domains need different embedding models.

Covered in post 3: Skill 1.4.3: Vector Search at Scale.

Skill 1.4.4: Connecting sources

[IMAGE: t1-4-4-exam.png — alt: "Exam scenarios for connectors: Confluence and SharePoint connectors, Web Crawler, custom data source, Secrets Manager, Amazon Q Business"]

Traps: writing a crawler for Confluence or SharePoint; manual exports that go stale; credentials in environment variables; building a dozen connectors when the scenario wants an assistant over many company apps.

Covered in post 4: Skill 1.4.4: Connect Wikis and Document Systems to a Knowledge Base (lab).

Skill 1.4.5: Keeping it fresh

[IMAGE: t1-4-5-exam.png — alt: "Exam scenarios for freshness: S3 event to Lambda to sync, scheduled sync, direct ingestion, deletions, new embedding model, incremental sync"]

Traps: recreating the knowledge base to refresh it; relying on events alone with no scheduled backstop; forgetting that deletions must reach the index; mixing vectors from two embedding models.

Covered in post 5: Skill 1.4.5: Keep the Vector Store Fresh (lab).

Keyword shortcuts for Task 1.4

  • “Managed RAG, least operational overhead” → Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases
  • “Precise matches but full-section context” → hierarchical chunking
  • “OpenSearch should call a Bedrock embedding model” → neural plugin + ML connector
  • “Existing PostgreSQL, join with business tables” → Aurora PostgreSQL + pgvector
  • “Billions of vectors, lowest storage cost” → Amazon S3 Vectors
  • “Status or ownership changes often” → DynamoDB metadata beside the vector store
  • “Only the current version”, “only this region” → metadata attributes + retrieval filter
  • “Recall too low” → raise ef_search
  • “Index doesn't fit in memory” → quantization or disk-based vector search
  • “More queries per second” → replicas
  • “Confluence, SharePoint, Salesforce, website” → Knowledge Bases connectors
  • “System with no connector”, “searchable in seconds” → custom data source + direct ingestion
  • “Keep the index current as files change” → S3 event → Lambda → StartIngestionJob, plus a schedule

Practice questions for Task 1.4 will be added in a later post. Until then, the official AWS Skill Builder practice question set is the closest thing to the real exam.
